workflow_metadata.name: Systems Engineering & Architecture Workflow
workflow_metadata.description: Design and validate complete system architecture, create machine-readable architecture products
workflow_metadata.created_from: decision_flow.json v2.5.0 - extracted Arch-02 through Arch-05
workflow_metadata.purpose: Create UAF-based service_architecture.json for each service and generate system_of_systems_graph.json

from_setup.description: Standard entry after completing setup workflow

context_management.description: Prevent context drift and token exhaustion during workflow execution

rag_enhanced_mode.description: RECOMMENDED - Use RAG for automatic context injection and degradation detection
rag_enhanced_mode.benefits: Automatic context refresh, degradation detection, token-efficient retrieval
rag_enhanced_mode.fallback: If RAG not set up, use manual operations counter and refresh sequence below

operations_counter.rule: Increment after each real operation (file creation, tool execution, artifact generation)

degradation_signals_watch_for: Asking about system name (it's in working_memory.json)

3. SAVE STATE - Update working_memory.json and step_progress_tracker.json
4. RELOAD - Read workflow file, architectural_definitions.json, templates

self_improvement.description: Continuous workflow improvement through observation and metrics

workflow_steps.name: System Analysis & Service Decomposition
workflow_steps.description: Analyze system requirements and decompose into services

actions.purpose: Parse feature requirements and identify required systems/services
Determine if this is a single service, multi-service system, or system-of-systems
Break down system into logical services based on business capabilities
guidance: Ensure services are cohesive and loosely coupled

workflow_steps.name: Service Architecture Specification
workflow_steps.description: Create UAF-based service_architecture.json for each service
workflow_steps.maps_from: Arch-02, Arch-03: Service architecture creation and validation

actions.description: For each service, create VERSIONED service_architecture.json

semantic_versioning.major: Breaking interface changes, fundamental architecture changes

symlink_creation.purpose: Tools use symlink to always reference latest version

actions.preservation_rule: NEVER delete old versions - they are historical record and enable rollback

actions.purpose: Detailed specification of each component within services
Catalog all interfaces between services and external systems

actions.description: Assign ports and create port registry (CONDITIONAL - only for IT systems)

condition.if_true: Execute port assignment and create port_registry.json
condition.if_false: Skip this action - non-IT systems don't need network ports

actions.purpose: Prevent port conflicts by assigning unique ports to each IT service upfront
actions.rationale: Port conflicts cause 'Address already in use' errors during deployment. Solving this architecturally prevents operational issues. Only applicable to IT systems with network services.

port_assignment_strategy.step_2: Assign primary port based on category range (app:8000-8099, internal:8100-8199, etc.)
port_assignment_strategy.step_4: Assign secondary ports if needed (metrics: 9000+, admin: localhost only)
port_assignment_strategy.step_5: Update each service_architecture.json -> deployment.ports with assigned port
port_assignment_strategy.step_6: Create/update port_registry.json with complete port mapping

validation.must_pass: No port conflicts allowed before proceeding to development

required_fields: binding (0.0.0.0 for all interfaces, 127.0.0.1 for localhost only)

docker_implications.conflict_prevention: Port registry ensures no two containers map to same host port

actions.description: Create security architecture (CONDITIONAL - required for IT systems with human users)

condition.check: framework_id == 'uaf' AND system has human users OR external API access
condition.if_true: Create security_architecture.json with authentication, authorization, and security controls
condition.if_false: Skip - internal machine-to-machine systems may have lighter security requirements
condition.user_detection: Check if any service has 'user_facing: true' OR 'external_api: true' in service_architecture.json

actions.purpose: Define comprehensive security architecture UPFRONT - authentication, authorization, API gateway, rate limiting, encryption, audit logging
actions.rationale: IT systems in modern, interconnected world must prioritize security from the start. Retrofitting security is expensive and risky.
required_sections: encryption (in-transit TLS, at-rest AES-256, key management)
human_user_scenarios: Web application with end users → REQUIRED
Internal microservices only → OPTIONAL (lighter security acceptable)

upfront_emphasis.critical: Security is NOT an afterthought. Design authentication and authorization flows BEFORE implementing any service.
upfront_emphasis.blocking: Security architecture must be reviewed and approved before SE-03 validation gate
upfront_emphasis.user_experience_impact: Poor security UX (complex auth flows, unclear errors) leads to user abandonment and support tickets

actions.description: Create deployment architecture (CONDITIONAL - required for IT systems)

condition.if_true: Create deployment_architecture.json emphasizing ease and simplicity
condition.if_false: Skip - non-IT systems (biology, ecology) don't have deployment infrastructure

actions.purpose: Design deployment for EASE, SIMPLICITY, and STRAIGHTFORWARD operation. Enable one-command deployment and rapid rollback.
actions.rationale: Complex deployment processes slow iteration, increase errors, and frustrate developers. Deployment simplicity is a competitive advantage.
required_sections: orchestration (docker-compose OR kubernetes - choose simpler option)
ci_cd_pipeline (build, test, deploy stages, automated testing)

simplicity_first_principle.default: Use Docker Compose unless Kubernetes features absolutely necessary
simplicity_first_principle.one_command: System MUST deploy with single command: 'docker-compose up -d' or 'kubectl apply -f manifests/'
simplicity_first_principle.quick_start_time: Target: New developer can deploy entire system in < 10 minutes from git clone
simplicity_first_principle.documentation: README.md must have step-by-step deployment instructions with expected outputs

upfront_emphasis.critical: Deployment complexity is NOT deferred to later. Design for ease of deployment NOW to enable rapid iteration.
upfront_emphasis.blocking: Deployment architecture must be validated before development begins
upfront_emphasis.developer_experience_impact: If deployment is painful, developers avoid testing integrated system → integration bugs discovered late

actions.description: Create UX and API design architecture (CONDITIONAL - required for IT systems with human users or external APIs)

condition.check: framework_id == 'uaf' AND (system has human users OR external API consumers)
condition.if_true: Create ux_api_design.json with user experience principles and API design standards
condition.if_false: Skip - internal machine-to-machine systems may not need user-facing design
condition.user_detection: Check if any service has 'user_facing: true' OR 'external_api: true' OR 'api_gateway' service exists

actions.purpose: Ensure STRAIGHTFORWARD and POSITIVE user experience. Design intuitive APIs, clear error messages, comprehensive documentation.
actions.rationale: Poor UX leads to user abandonment, support burden, and negative reputation. API design affects every integration and can't be easily changed.
required_sections: rest_api_design (resource modeling, query params, pagination, filtering)
error_handling (user-friendly messages, validation errors, recovery guidance)
api_documentation (OpenAPI spec, interactive docs, getting started guide, code examples)
versioning_strategy (url_path versioning, deprecation policy, migration guide)
authentication_ux (clear auth flow, token management, sandbox environment)

api_gateway_requirement.mandatory: If system has human users OR external APIs, api_gateway service MUST exist
responsibilities: Single entry point (unified base URL: https://api.example.com)
api_gateway_requirement.orphaned_service_prevention: api_gateway MUST be implemented, not just scaffolding. Validate in SE-06 graph analysis.

user_experience_targets.time_to_first_success: New user completes first successful action in < 5 minutes
user_experience_targets.api_time_to_first_call: Developer makes first successful API call in < 5 minutes from reading docs
user_experience_targets.task_success_rate: > 95% of users complete common tasks without support
user_experience_targets.error_recovery: Errors provide actionable guidance, not just failure messages

upfront_emphasis.critical: UX is NOT polish added later. Core user flows and API contracts designed NOW prevent costly refactoring.
upfront_emphasis.blocking: UX and API design must be reviewed before implementation
upfront_emphasis.modern_world_requirement: IT systems compete on user experience. Clunky APIs and confusing UX lose users to competitors.

outputs: specs/machine/ux_api_design.json (if UAF with human users/external APIs)

workflow_steps.name: Constraints & Template Validation
workflow_steps.description: Validate all service architectures against templates and constraints

actions.description: Run architecture validation for each service
actions.purpose: Ensure service_architecture.json complies with template
validation_checks: All required sections present
UAF 1.2 compliance
JSON schema validation
Referential integrity

actions.description: Issue Resolution Loop - Fix validation errors iteratively
actions.pattern: MANDATORY LOOP - Do not skip this

loop_structure.step_2: Capture and analyze ALL errors and warnings from tool output
loop_structure.step_3: Categorize issues (missing sections, type errors, UAF violations, referential integrity)
loop_structure.step_4: Fix issues by category (see common_issues below)
loop_structure.step_6: If errors remain, LOOP back to step_2
loop_structure.step_7: If validation passes (zero errors), move to next service
loop_structure.termination: Loop continues until zero errors OR max 5 iterations (then escalate to user)

common_issues_and_fixes.fix: Add section from template, populate with service-specific content
Fix JSON syntax errors, ensure valid brackets/braces/commas
common_issues_and_fixes.verification: Use JSON validator before re-running architecture validation

common_issues_and_fixes.fix: Review definitions/architectural_definitions.json for UAF requirements, update architecture accordingly
common_issues_and_fixes.examples: Wrong classification, missing mandatory fields, incorrect nesting

common_issues_and_fixes.issue: Referential integrity error (interface not found in registry)
common_issues_and_fixes.fix: Either add missing interface to interface_registry.json OR correct interface reference in service_architecture.json

common_issues_and_fixes.issue: Type mismatch (field expects array but got string)
common_issues_and_fixes.fix: Correct field type to match template schema

common_issues_and_fixes.issue: Empty or placeholder values in required fields
common_issues_and_fixes.fix: Replace placeholders with actual architectural decisions
common_issues_and_fixes.examples: REPLACE_WITH_X, TBD, TODO must be replaced with real values

llm_agent_instructions: DO NOT proceed to next service until current service passes validation
DO NOT skip errors - every error must be fixed
DO NOT assume validation passes - always check tool output
READ the actual error messages from validate_architecture.py carefully
If same error appears 3+ times, re-read template and definitions to understand requirement
Track iteration count - if exceeding 5 iterations, review your approach
actions.success_criteria: validate_architecture.py returns zero errors for the service

actions.description: Validate port registry for conflicts (CONDITIONAL - only if port_registry.json exists)

condition.if_false: Skip this action - port registry not applicable for non-IT systems
condition.note: This action only runs if SE-02-A04 was executed (i.e., port_registry.json exists)

actions.purpose: Ensure no port conflicts exist before development begins (IT systems only)
validation_checks: PC-01: No duplicate primary ports across services
PC-02: No port overlap between any service ports (primary, metrics, admin)
PC-03: Ports within designated ranges (app:8000-8099, internal:8100-8199, etc.)
PC-04: Avoid privileged ports below 1024
PC-05: Docker host-container port mapping consistency

duplicate_primary_ports.symptom: Two services assigned same primary port (e.g., both on 8000)
duplicate_primary_ports.fix: Reassign second service to next available port in range

metrics_conflicts_with_primary.symptom: Service A metrics port (9001) conflicts with Service B primary (9001)
metrics_conflicts_with_primary.fix: Shift metrics ports to separate range or use primary+1000 pattern

well_known_port_conflicts.symptom: Service assigned port 5432 conflicts with PostgreSQL
well_known_port_conflicts.fix: Check third_party_defaults in port_ranges, avoid those ports
well_known_port_conflicts.prevention: Reserve well-known ports for their intended services

actions.blocking: Yes - port conflicts MUST be resolved before development
actions.rationale: Catching port conflicts now prevents 'Address already in use' errors during deployment and testing phases

actions.description: Validate security architecture (CONDITIONAL - if security_architecture.json exists)

condition.if_true: Validate security architecture for completeness and best practices
condition.if_false: Skip - security architecture not required for internal-only systems

validation_checks: Authentication strategy defined and appropriate for user types
Authorization model (RBAC/ABAC) complete with roles and permissions
API gateway configuration includes SSL/TLS, CORS, rate limiting
Rate limiting strategy defined with specific limits
Input validation covers XSS and SQL injection prevention
Encryption specified for both in-transit (TLS 1.2+) and at-rest (AES-256)
Audit logging configured with retention policy and alerting
Security testing approach defined (SAST, dependency scanning)

weak_authentication.symptom: No MFA for privileged users, weak password policy
weak_authentication.fix: Enable MFA for admin roles, enforce strong password requirements
weak_authentication.security_impact: HIGH - weak auth leads to account compromise

missing_api_gateway.fix: Add api_gateway service, route all external traffic through it
missing_api_gateway.security_impact: CRITICAL - no centralized auth, rate limiting, or request validation

insufficient_rate_limiting.symptom: No rate limits or very high limits
insufficient_rate_limiting.fix: Define reasonable per-user and per-IP limits (e.g., 100 req/min)
insufficient_rate_limiting.security_impact: MEDIUM - vulnerable to DoS and brute force attacks

no_encryption_at_rest.fix: Identify sensitive fields (passwords, PII, tokens), encrypt with AES-256
no_encryption_at_rest.security_impact: HIGH - data breach exposes sensitive information

review_questions: Is the authentication flow simple enough for users to understand?
Are error messages helpful without exposing security details?
Is the security approach proportional to the threat model?
Are there clear procedures for security incidents?
Is secret management automated and secure?
actions.success_criteria: Security architecture addresses all threat vectors, follows industry best practices, and provides positive UX
actions.blocking: Yes - security gaps MUST be addressed before development
actions.rationale: Security vulnerabilities discovered after implementation are 10x more expensive to fix than during design

actions.description: Validate deployment architecture (CONDITIONAL - if deployment_architecture.json exists)

condition.if_true: Validate deployment architecture for ease and completeness
condition.if_false: Skip - deployment architecture not required for non-IT systems

validation_checks: Deployment philosophy emphasizes simplicity and ease
One-command deployment strategy defined (docker-compose up -d OR kubectl apply)
Containerization with Docker/Podman using official base images
Orchestration choice justified (docker-compose for simplicity OR kubernetes for scale)
CI/CD pipeline defined with build, test, deploy stages
Environment management covers dev, staging, production with parity
Service discovery mechanism defined (DNS, health checks)
Monitoring and observability strategy complete (metrics, logging, alerting)
Backup and disaster recovery with defined RTO/RPO

overcomplicated_orchestration.symptom: Using Kubernetes for 3-service system that doesn't need it
overcomplicated_orchestration.fix: Simplify to docker-compose unless scale/HA features truly needed

no_health_checks.fix: Add health check endpoints to all services, configure in orchestrator
no_health_checks.impact: Can't detect service failures, no automated recovery

manual_deployment_steps.symptom: Deployment requires multiple manual commands or configuration
manual_deployment_steps.fix: Automate in single command or script, document in README
manual_deployment_steps.impact: Error-prone deployments, slow onboarding for new developers

no_rollback_strategy.symptom: No defined procedure to revert failed deployments
no_rollback_strategy.fix: Define rollback command/procedure, test it works

missing_observability.symptom: No metrics, logging, or alerting defined
missing_observability.fix: Add Prometheus metrics, centralized logging, critical alerts
missing_observability.impact: Can't diagnose issues, blind to system health

review_questions: Can a new developer deploy the entire system in < 10 minutes?
Is the deployment process documented step-by-step in README?
Is rollback simple and fast (< 5 minutes)?
Are health checks comprehensive enough to detect failures?
Is the infrastructure reproducible (IaC) or manual?
Are there clear procedures for scaling up/down?
actions.success_criteria: Deployment is simple, automated, well-documented, and enables rapid iteration
actions.blocking: Yes - complex or undocumented deployment will slow development and increase errors
actions.rationale: Deployment ease directly impacts development velocity and system reliability

actions.description: Validate UX and API design architecture (CONDITIONAL - if ux_api_design.json exists)

condition.if_true: Validate UX and API design for clarity, consistency, and developer-friendliness
condition.if_false: Skip - UX/API design not required for internal machine-to-machine systems

validation_checks: UX philosophy defined with clear user types and goals
API design principles follow REST/GraphQL best practices
API endpoints follow consistent naming and structure
Error handling provides user-friendly messages with recovery guidance
API documentation includes OpenAPI spec, interactive docs, code examples
Versioning strategy defined (url_path recommended) with deprecation policy
Performance targets set (p50, p95, p99 latency)
Rate limiting transparent with clear headers and error messages
Authentication UX is simple with clear token management
API gateway defined with responsibilities (auth, rate limiting, routing)

inconsistent_api_design.symptom: Some endpoints use camelCase, others snake_case; mixed naming conventions
inconsistent_api_design.fix: Standardize on single convention (snake_case recommended), document in API design
inconsistent_api_design.impact: Developer confusion, harder to use API

poor_error_messages.symptom: Errors like '500 Internal Server Error' or technical jargon
poor_error_messages.fix: Return helpful messages: 'Email is required. Please provide your email address.'
poor_error_messages.impact: Users can't recover from errors, support burden increases

missing_api_documentation.symptom: No OpenAPI spec, no interactive docs, no code examples
missing_api_documentation.fix: Create OpenAPI 3.0 spec, generate Swagger UI docs, add curl/Python/JS examples
missing_api_documentation.impact: Developers can't use API without extensive trial and error

no_api_gateway.symptom: Services exposed directly, no unified entry point
no_api_gateway.fix: Add api_gateway service, route all traffic through single base URL
no_api_gateway.impact: Inconsistent auth, can't enforce rate limits, poor observability

api_gateway_not_implemented.symptom: api_gateway defined in architecture but only scaffolding exists (orphaned service)
api_gateway_not_implemented.fix: Implement api_gateway with routing, auth, rate limiting, SSL termination
api_gateway_not_implemented.impact: CRITICAL - system non-functional without working gateway

unclear_versioning.symptom: No versioning strategy or using query params/headers (hard to discover)
unclear_versioning.fix: Use url_path versioning (/api/v1/users) - most visible and explicit
unclear_versioning.impact: Breaking changes break all clients, no migration path

review_questions: Can a developer make their first successful API call in < 5 minutes from reading docs?
Are error messages helpful and actionable, not just technical failures?
Is the API consistent and predictable across all endpoints?
Does the system have a working API gateway (not just scaffolding)?
Is API documentation complete with examples for common use cases?
Can users easily obtain and manage API tokens/credentials?
Are rate limits clearly communicated with headers and documentation?
Is the UX simple enough for target user skill level?

api_gateway_validation.critical: If api_gateway service exists in architecture, validate it will be FULLY IMPLEMENTED, not orphaned
api_gateway_validation.check_in_SE_06: system_of_systems_graph_v2.py with --analyze-issues will detect orphaned services
api_gateway_validation.prevention: Mark api_gateway as critical path service, validate implementation in Development workflow

actions.success_criteria: UX and API design enables users to succeed quickly with minimal friction
actions.blocking: Yes - poor UX/API design decisions are expensive to fix after launch
actions.rationale: User experience determines adoption, retention, and competitive advantage

gates.name: Architecture Validation Gate
checks: Port registry validated with zero port conflicts (if applicable to framework)
Security architecture validated (if UAF with human users) - BLOCKING
Deployment architecture validated (if UAF/IT system) - BLOCKING
UX and API design validated (if UAF with human users/external APIs) - BLOCKING

conditional_checks.port_registry_validation: Only required if deployment_characteristics.port_management_applicable == true (i.e., UAF framework)
conditional_checks.security_architecture_validation: Required if framework_id == 'uaf' AND (human users OR external APIs)
conditional_checks.ux_api_design_validation: Required if framework_id == 'uaf' AND (human users OR external APIs)

upfront_emphasis_gate.purpose: Enforce that security, deployment ease, and UX are designed UPFRONT, not as afterthoughts
upfront_emphasis_gate.blocking_rationale: IT systems in modern, interconnected world MUST prioritize security, ease of deployment, and positive user experience from the start
modern_world_requirements: Security: Authentication, authorization, encryption, audit logging designed before any code written
Deployment: One-command deployment, automated rollback, comprehensive monitoring designed before development
UX: Intuitive APIs, clear errors, comprehensive docs designed before implementation
API Gateway: If human users/external APIs, gateway MUST exist and be fully implemented (not orphaned)
upfront_emphasis_gate.cost_of_retrofitting: Fixing security vulnerabilities, complex deployments, or poor UX after launch is 10-100x more expensive than designing correctly upfront

actions.description: Map logical components to deployment units

workflow_steps.description: Ensure all specifications are consistent and complete

actions.purpose: Ensure interfaces between services are consistently defined on both sides
Ensure architecture aligns with foundational documents
checks: All user scenarios covered by architecture

actions.purpose: Detect potential architectural issues (circular dependencies, missing interfaces, etc.)

workflow_steps.name: System Graph Generation
workflow_steps.maps_from: Part of Arch-06, extracted for machine-readable artifacts

actions.description: Create index.json (points to symlinks for latest versions)
actions.purpose: Catalog all machine-readable architecture artifacts using symlinks
includes: Service list with paths to service_architecture.json SYMLINKS (not versioned files)

path_format.note: Path points to symlink, which points to latest versioned file
path_format.benefit: Tools always use latest version without updating index.json

actions.description: Generate and Validate system_of_systems_graph.json with framework-specific analysis selection
actions.purpose: Create framework-agnostic graph with comprehensive NetworkX analysis and validation

analysis_selection_guidance.step_4: Select analyses based on framework recommendations (high_priority + medium_priority as appropriate)
analysis_selection_guidance.step_5: Check if any selected analyses require edge weights (e.g., flow analysis)
analysis_selection_guidance.step_6: If edge weights required but missing: either add weights to architecture files OR skip that analysis
analysis_selection_guidance.step_7: Construct command with appropriate flags: --centrality --community --cycles --scc --dag --flow etc.
analysis_selection_guidance.step_8: Update working_memory.json -> analysis_configuration with selected analyses

framework_specific_examples.uaf: --centrality --dag --scc --community --connectivity (verifies no circular deps, finds critical services)

edge_weight_guidance.when_needed: Flow analysis REQUIRES edge weights. Other analyses benefit from weights but work without them.
edge_weight_guidance.how_to_add: Add 'weight' field to each interface/interaction/relationship in architecture files

inputs: All architecture files (service_architecture.json, component_architecture.json, etc via symlinks)

validation_loop.description: CRITICAL - This tool doesn't just generate a file, it VALIDATES the system architecture
validation_loop.step_1: Select appropriate analyses based on framework (see analysis_selection_guidance above)
validation_loop.step_2: Run system_of_systems_graph_v2.py with selected analysis flags
validation_loop.step_3: Examine tool output for errors, warnings, and inconsistencies
validation_loop.step_4: Analyze generated graph for system-level issues
validation_loop.step_5: Fix issues in source architecture files (architecture.json files or interface_registry.json)
validation_loop.step_7: If issues remain, LOOP back to step_3
validation_loop.step_8: If graph generation succeeds with zero errors/warnings, proceed
validation_loop.termination: Loop until clean OR max 5 iterations (then escalate to user)

system_level_issues_to_check.detection: Tool may report circular dependency chains or graph shows cycles
system_level_issues_to_check.fix: Refactor service boundaries to break circular dependency - one service must not depend on the other, or introduce event-driven decoupling
system_level_issues_to_check.architectural_principle: Services should form a DAG (directed acyclic graph)

system_level_issues_to_check.detection: Service A calls interface X on Service B, but Service B doesn't expose interface X
system_level_issues_to_check.fix: Either add missing interface to Service B's architecture OR correct Service A's dependency declaration
system_level_issues_to_check.cross_reference: Check interface_registry.json and service dependencies sections

system_level_issues_to_check.detection: Graph references interface but interface_registry.json doesn't contain it
system_level_issues_to_check.fix: Add interface definition to interface_registry.json with complete contract
system_level_issues_to_check.ensure: Interface has request/response schemas, authentication requirements, protocols

system_level_issues_to_check.detection: Two services reference same interface but with different version requirements
system_level_issues_to_check.fix: Align interface versions OR clearly document version compatibility requirements
system_level_issues_to_check.version_strategy: Use semantic versioning to manage compatibility

system_level_issues_to_check.issue: Orphaned services (no incoming or outgoing dependencies)
system_level_issues_to_check.detection: Service appears in system but has no connections to other services
system_level_issues_to_check.fix: Either connect service to system OR remove if it's not actually part of this system
system_level_issues_to_check.validate: Every service should have a clear role in at least one user scenario

system_level_issues_to_check.detection: Multiple services define same entity with different schemas
system_level_issues_to_check.fix: Establish canonical data model ownership - one service owns entity definition, others reference it
system_level_issues_to_check.pattern: Follow domain-driven design bounded context principles

system_level_issues_to_check.detection: Services depend on external systems not declared in external_systems
system_level_issues_to_check.fix: Add external system to system-level external_systems list with integration details

system_level_issues_to_check.detection: Public-facing service directly accessing database service without auth layer
system_level_issues_to_check.fix: Introduce security boundaries - authentication/authorization services between public and private services
system_level_issues_to_check.principle: Defense in depth - multiple security layers

system_level_issues_to_check.detection: Service uses async HTTP framework (python_uvicorn: true) but interfaces suggest synchronous database operations (SQLAlchemy without async, psycopg2, pymongo)
system_level_issues_to_check.fix: Align async/sync patterns: async HTTP frameworks (uvicorn/FastAPI) should use async database drivers (asyncpg, motor, async SQLAlchemy) to avoid blocking the event loop
system_level_issues_to_check.architectural_principle: Async frameworks require async I/O throughout the stack - mixing sync DB with async HTTP blocks the event loop and degrades performance

common_async_drivers.PostgreSQL: asyncpg or databases library with async SQLAlchemy

fix_instructions: 1. Check architecture_issues.json for specific services with async/sync mismatches
2. For each flagged service, update service_architecture.json interfaces section
3. Update interface descriptions to explicitly specify async database drivers
4. Example: Change 'Internal database for character entities unique to this service' to 'Internal async database (asyncpg) for character entities'

llm_agent_instructions: STEP 1: Select analyses appropriate for your framework - see analysis_selection_guidance above
STEP 2: Check if flow analysis is needed - if yes, ensure edge weights are included in architecture files
STEP 3: Construct command with framework-appropriate analysis flags (e.g., for UAF: --centrality --dag --scc --community)
STEP 4: Run system_of_systems_graph_v2.py with selected flags, --detect-gaps, and --analyze-issues
STEP 5: READ the tool output carefully - it contains valuable graph analysis results
STEP 6: Review architecture_issues.json for architectural problems (circular deps, orphans, async/sync issues)
STEP 7: Review knowledge_gaps section for missing nodes or edges ("dark matter" components)
STEP 8: Update working_memory.json -> analysis_configuration with selected analyses and rationale
DO NOT just run the tool and assume success - ANALYZE the results
DO NOT proceed if tool reports errors - fix them first
CRITICAL: async HTTP services MUST use async database drivers (check async_sync_consistency)
Use NetworkX analysis results to validate architecture quality (centrality, clustering, modularity)
success_criteria: Framework-appropriate analyses selected and run successfully
Generated graph shows cohesive system (no orphans, no unexplained cycles)
All interfaces properly connected between components
NetworkX analysis results make sense for this system type
Knowledge gap detection reveals no critical missing components

version_indexes.name: latest

update_pattern.initial_creation: Add entry for each service at v1.0.0-{date}
update_pattern.on_update: Add new version entry, update latest_version field

actions.verification: All required machine-readable files present and valid

workflow_steps.note: For architecture updates, see SE-07 (optional); for mixed-version testing, see SE-08 (optional)

workflow_steps.name: Architecture Evolution (OPTIONAL - For Updates)
workflow_steps.description: Update existing architecture with proper versioning

completion.description: Systems engineering & architecture workflow complete - all machine-readable artifacts created

critical_reminders: ALWAYS use absolute paths from working_memory.json for tool invocations
Run validate_architecture.py after creating each service_architecture.json
Ensure UAF 1.2 compliance for all architecture artifacts
system_of_systems_graph.py requires index.json to be created first
Do not skip validation gates - they prevent downstream issues
validation_loop_critical: VALIDATION TOOLS ARE NOT OPTIONAL - They are the centerpiece of workflow quality
DO NOT just run validation tools and move on - FIX ALL ISSUES they discover
MANDATORY: Use issue resolution loops in SE-03-A03 and SE-06-A02
READ tool output carefully - errors and warnings indicate real problems
ITERATE until validation passes with ZERO errors - not 'mostly works'
Each validation failure is an architectural issue that MUST be resolved
validate_architecture.py: Fix service-level issues (missing sections, type errors, UAF violations)
system_of_systems_graph.py: Fix system-level issues (circular deps, interface mismatches, orphaned services)
Maximum 5 iterations per validation loop - if exceeding, escalate to user for guidance
Success criteria: Tool completes with zero errors AND architecture makes logical sense

validate_architecture.py.pattern: Run → Analyze errors → Fix → Re-run → Verify clean
validate_architecture.py.do_not: Skip errors, assume validation passes, proceed with warnings
validate_architecture.py.common_fixes: Add missing sections, fix JSON syntax, correct UAF violations, resolve referential integrity

system_of_systems_graph.py.when: After all services defined and index.json created
system_of_systems_graph.py.pattern: Run → Analyze graph and output → Fix system-level issues → Re-run → Verify coherence
system_of_systems_graph.py.do_not: Just check that file was created, ignore warnings, skip graph analysis
system_of_systems_graph.py.common_fixes: Break circular dependencies, add missing interfaces, fix interface mismatches, connect orphaned services

common_mistakes: Running validation tools but not fixing issues they find
Assuming validation passed without checking tool output
Proceeding with validation warnings or errors
Not iterating validation loops until clean
Not analyzing system_of_systems_graph.json for coherence issues
quality_gates_mandatory: G-SE-03: Architecture Validation Gate (BLOCKING - validates all architectures pass)
G-SE-05: Specification Completeness Gate (BLOCKING - validates consistency)
G-SE-06: Architecture Completion Gate (BLOCKING - validates system coherence)
